reason: (1) A bucket of an affine x-filter is a union of p/M vertical lines x=c, i.e. lines of one parallel class (a pencil through the point at infinity). Szemeredi-Trotter-type bounds, including Stevens-de Zeeuw I<<(PL)^{11/15} and arbitrary-field variants, give nothing new for a parallel family: incidences between a point set and a parallel pencil are exactly the fibre sizes, which sum to |P| with no saving. The bilinear structure has to come from the chord lines through pairs of base points, not from the bucket lines. Chord-line incidences count collinear triples on E (P,Q,-(P+Q)). That is the group law, and it is simulable in the generic group model (closure: GGM-simulable incidence oracles, KN-FIND-b7e091). (2) The parameters are inconsistent. With P=B^2 sums and L=p/M bucket lines, the Stevens-de Zeeuw exponent bound (B^2*p/M)^{11/15} exceeds the trivial count B^2 whenever p/M>B^{8/11}, which covers the whole range beta<=0.7, M<=1024. So a theta in [2/5,7/10] cannot come out. (3) Toy data (p~2^25, B=1200, all pairwise sums x(P+Q) bucketed): max-bucket/(mean) for random F is 1.013/1.042/1.119 at M=16/256/1024 and for x-interval F is 1.009/1.052/1.129, which is Poisson fluctuation. Equidistribution already holds by Weil/character sums in this regime, so the ST bound adds nothing. Group-AP F={iP}: the sums take only 2B-1 distinct values with multiplicity <=B/2, so the excess over B^2/M is at most O(B)<<B^{3/2}. No shape saturates, and none needs ST. (4) Nongenericity: the affine filter reads the x-coordinate, so it is representation-dependent. But the quantity bounded is a bucket-load statistic. It does not change the decomposition oracle cost D or the factor base B, so the B*D^2 >= N certificate is unchanged and this is at most an accounting/variance device. G(M)=O(1) for affine filters is true, but it follows from Weil plus the trivial bound; it is a closure, not an advance.
